articles.abstract: The first code an adversary reaches when a peer speaks post-quantum cryptography is a decoder or a verifier: a server decapsulates a client's ML-KEM (Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism) ciphertext, a client verifies a server's ML-DSA (Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm) or SLH-DSA (Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Algorithm) signature, and both parse public keys from certificates. Implementation assessment for these National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standards has concentrated on known-answer vectors and constant-time analysis, not on hostile bytes. We fuzz the decode and verify paths of both Java implementations of the standards, Bouncy Castle and the Java Development Kit (JDK) providers since version 24, with two fuzzing methods and one pre-registered outcome oracle. A 900,000-input campaign against Bouncy Castle 1.85 produced zero anomalies. A null result is worthless without evidence the instrument could find a defect, so we add a positive control: Bouncy Castle 1.84 ships a real ML-DSA public-key decoder defect, no length validation, which the identical harness recovers in seconds. Run against three JDK releases with byte-identical inputs, the same instrument finds the same defect class again: the JDK's KeyFactory accepts an ML-DSA or ML-KEM public key of any length and checks the size only at use, where it fails closed. Both implementations decide alike on every shared input and differ only in where they check. Two lessons transfer: pairing-dependent defects need composed parse-then-use targets, and fast-throw exception elision silently blinds long Java virtual machine campaigns. All targets, harnesses and data are public.

articles.title: Ag/Al₂O₃/ITO memristor for honeybee-inspired associative learning, behavioral emulation, and conductance-constrained flower classification
articles.abstract: Honeybees identify floral cues and develop experience-dependent foraging behavior by associating odors with nectar rewards. Memristor conductance depends on prior stimulation and can be gradually tuned by electrical pulses, allowing changes in synaptic strength during learning to be represented electrically. Here, we fabricated an Ag/Al₂O₃/ITO memristor and examined how the compliance current and electrical pulses regulate its resistive-switching behavior and conductance states. Increasing the compliance current raised the low-resistance-state current while producing relatively little change in the high-resistance-state current, consistent with the progressive growth of an Ag conductive filament. Under pulsed stimulation, the device exhibited long-term potentiation and depression, paired-pulse facilitation, retention of well-separated resistance states for 103 s, and multilevel resistance modulation. Adjusting the pulse amplitude and sequence enabled the electrical emulation of Pavlovian conditioning, learning–forgetting–relearning, and graded states corresponding to sleep, drowsiness, and wakefulness. For flower classification, the weights of the CNN fully connected layer were mapped onto 50 discrete conductance states extracted from the experimentally measured LTP/LTD characteristics, whereas convolutional feature extraction remained in software. The conductance-mapped model achieved an accuracy of 86.55%, only 0.54 percentage points below the 87.09% obtained with the software model. These results show that different pulse protocols can produce distinct history-dependent responses within the same Ag/Al₂O₃/ITO device architecture, while the resulting device-derived conductance states can support device-constrained neural-network weight mapping.

articles.title: Multi-Physics Coupled Modeling and Predictive Control of the DLP Photocuring Printing Process
articles.abstract: To address the loss of forming quality caused by the strong multiphysics coupling in digital light processing (DLP)-based vat photopolymerization additive manufacturing, this study proposes an integrated framework incorporating multiphysics modeling, key parameter identification, and advanced control strategies. First, a nonlinear state-space model describing the coupled evolution of optical, chemical, thermal, and mechanical fields was established based on the Beer–Lambert law, curing kinetics, and one-dimensional transient heat conduction theory. Subsequently, the kinetic parameters were identified through ultraviolet differential scanning calorimetry (UV-DSC) experiments. An indirect validation method based on DSC heat-flow signals was further proposed, where a capture factor was introduced to map the equivalent heat flow, thereby verifying the correctness of the coupled heat-generation and heat-transfer terms in the model.At the control level, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) strategy integrated with a sliding mode observer (SMO) was developed, and a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network was introduced to assist prediction and improve real-time regulation performance. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) experiments and variable light-intensity strategies demonstrated that the proposed control system significantly improved curing uniformity along the thickness direction. Comparison with COMSOL simulations showed that the proposed model achieved prediction errors of only approximately 1% for both degree of cure and temperature, while also effectively predicting the warpage trend of printed structures. The results provide important theoretical support for achieving shape and property control in photopolymerization additive manufacturing processes.

articles.title: Quantum Fisher Information and Atom-EnvironmentEntanglement in a Moving Four-Level Atom Coupled to a KerrOptomechanical Cavity under a Magnetic Field
articles.abstract: We study phase-sensitive quantum dynamics in a hybrid cavity system consisting of a mov-ing four-level ladder atom, a quantized optical mode, and a mechanical oscillator. The atomicTransitions interact with the cavity field through a motion-dependent Jaynes-Cummings coupling.while radiation pressure couples the intracavity photons to the mechanical mode. A Kerr mediumprovides photon-number-dependent phase shifts, and an external magnetic �field generates Zeeman-shifted atomic sublevels. The quantum Fisher information and the von Neumann entropy of thereduced atomic states are used to follow the redistribution of phase information and the generationof atom�environment correlations. The results show that stronger hybrid coupling generally trans-fers locally accessible phase information away from the atom while increasing the mixedness of theatomic subsystem. Since the full state evolves unitarily, the reduced atomic entropy also quantifiesthe entanglement between the atom and the combined field mechanics sector. Kerr nonlinearityreorganizes this information �flow and can produce delayed loss of phase sensitivity or partial recoveryseries at selected times. The work highlights why quantum Fisher information and von NeumannEntropy must be interpreted together when metrological usefulness and entanglement are studied.in hybrid light-matter systems.
authors: S. Abdul Khali S. Abdul Khali
M. Khalid Khan M. Khalid Khan

articles.title: Synergistic Coagulation-Adsorption of Methyl Orange Dye Using DCD-F Resin and PAC-AC-CP Composite: Mechanisms and Techno-Economic Performance
articles.abstract: This study investigated the synergistic removal of methyl orange (MO) dye from synthetic textile wastewater using an integrated coagulation-adsorption system comprising dicyandiamide-formaldehyde (DCD-F) resin and a composite of polyaluminium chloride (PAC), activated carbon (AC), and cationic polymer (CP), denoted PAC-AC-CP, at a 70:25:5 mole ratio. Batch experiments were conducted using a conventional jar test to optimise DCD-F resin dosage and rapid mixing speed. The optimum conditions of 120 ppm DCD-F resin, 250 ppm PAC-AC-CP composite, and 180 rpm rapid mixing achieved 99% MO dye removal, reducing the colour value from 1622 ± 14.00 to 9 ± 2.02 ADMI. The final colour value was below the Malaysian industrial effluent discharge limits for Standard A and Standard B. Kinetic analysis showed that the pseudo-second-order (PSO) model provided the best fit, with R² values above 0.999. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) showed rough, porous, and aggregated flocs, while Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy indicated functional group interactions between MO dye and the treatment agents. Zeta potential shifted from − 20.6 to + 5.62 mV, supporting charge neutralisation and particle destabilisation. The findings indicate that MO dye removal involved charge neutralisation, adsorption, interparticle bridging, and sweep flocculation. A preliminary techno-economic analysis estimated a treatment cost of USD 0.5429/m³ at a capacity of 1,000 m³/day, indicating the potential of the proposed system for effective and economically feasible textile wastewater treatment.

articles.title: Chitin-like Hollow Alumina Nano-adsorbent for Remediation of Arsenate- contaminated Water: Synthesis by Double Reversed-phase Microemulsion Method and Study of Enhanced Arsenate-removal Ability and Mechanism
articles.abstract: Arsenic contamination in aquatic systems threatens ecosystems and human health. Chitin-like hollow alumina nanospheres were synthesized via a W/O/W microemulsion system with sodium meta-aluminate and NH₄HCO₃ as aqueous phases, and n-hexane with span-80 as oil phase. Precipitate was filtered, washed, freeze-dried to get precursor NH₄Al(OH)₂CO₃ (AACH), then calcined at 500°C for 3 h to obtain Al₂O₃ nano-adsorbent, characterized by XRD, SEM, TEM, and FTIR. Its adsorption performance and mechanism for arsenate ions (AsO43−, i.e., As(V)) were investigated based on batch adsorption experiments as well as adsorption thermodynamics and kinetics simulations. The optimization of synthesis conditions revealed that the Al2O3 nano-adsorbent synthesized with 0.94 M NH4HCO3 and 0.5 g span-80 at the reaction temperature of 45°C and calcination temperature of 500°C was of chitin-like hollow nanosphere morphology with a specific surface area of 394.99 m²/g and an average pore size of 4.46 nm. It exhibited the highest removal rate of 98.69% for As(V) in the solution of pH 3.0 while its As-removal ability increased with increasing dosage. Besides, the adsorption isotherm and adsorption kinetics for As(V) over Al2O3 nano-adsorbent at 298 K were in accordance with the Langmuir isotherm adsorption model and the pseudo-second order kinetic equation, with saturated adsorption capacity and correlation coefficient of 37.11 mg/g and 99.8%, respectively. In addition, Al2O3 nano-adsorbent retained good removal ability for As(V) during 30 day of consecutive desorption experiments, showing promising potential for the rapid and efficient remediation of As-contaminated water.

articles.title: The Dynamical Nature of the Historical Cycle: A Civilizational Evolution Perspective from the Collective Consciousness Field
articles.abstract: The historical cycle—the wave-like recurrence of dynastic rise and fall, civilizational flourishing and decline, and social transformation—is one of the most perplexing and inescapable phenomena of human civilization. Drawing upon the concept of the Collective Consciousness Field within Yuanling Theory, this paper proposes that the historical cycle is not an incomprehensible vortex of fate, but a dynamical necessity of the Collective Consciousness Field governed by principles such as Energy Balance, Frequency Resonance, Will Intensity, and Interactive Evolvability. The paper systematically expounds the ontological foundation of civilization as a Collective Consciousness Field, reveals the intrinsic mechanisms of social energy accumulation, cultural interface rigidification, critical phase transition, and civilizational reconstruction, and analyzes the dynamical nature of phase transitions including violent revolution, non-violent transformation, and gradual reform. It further argues that every historical reconstruction constitutes a civilizational leap—purging decay, restructuring interfaces, and ascending in dimensionality. This paper contends that as more individuals consciously optimize their own consciousness structures and participate in the construction of the Collective Consciousness Field, human civilization may have the potential to break free from the old cycle of “chaos and order” and advance toward a new epoch of self-organized, orderly, and creative resonance within the Collective Consciousness Field.

articles.title: Non-monotonic Plasmon-Induced Transparency in Asymmetric Terahertz Metasurfaces Integrated with Vanadium Dioxide
articles.abstract: Non-monotonic plasmon-induced transparency (PIT) is investigated in an asymmetric terahertz metasurface integrated with vanadium dioxide (VO₂) using full-wave electromagnetic simulations and coupled-mode theory (CMT). The unit cell consists of two vertical Au bars and one horizontal Au bar, with a VO₂ element positioned in the near-field coupling region. Under normally incident y-polarized THz excitation, the pair of vertical resonators supports a directly excited bright mode, whereas the horizontal resonator supports an indirectly excited dark mode. Gap asymmetry controls the near-field coupling between these modes, thereby enabling the formation and tuning of a pronounced PIT window. At a VO₂ conductivity of σ = 30 S/m and an asymmetry parameter of aₛ = 10 µm, two transmission minima at 1.09 and 1.20 THz are separated by a transparency peak at 1.13 THz. As the VO₂ conductivity increases, the PIT response exhibits a distinctly non-monotonic spectral evolution: the low-conductivity transparency window is progressively suppressed in the intermediate-conductivity regime and subsequently re-emerges at a substantially lower frequency in the high-conductivity state. Electromagnetic-field distributions reveal a conductivity-dependent redistribution of the coupled modal response. A conductivity-dependent two-mode CMT model reproduces this spectral evolution and indicates that it originates from the combined variations in bright–dark coupling, modal damping, and resonance detuning, rather than from an increase in ohmic loss alone. These findings provide a physical basis for reconfigurable THz filtering and multistate spectral modulation.

articles.title: Analog Neuromorphic Systems for Implantable Neural Interfaces
articles.abstract: With the increasing popularity of brain-machine interfaces for a variety of motor disorders and fundamental neuroscientific experiments, there is also a growth in new sensors with increasing number of parallel channels to sense brain activity. Hence, there is an urgent need to manage the exploding datarate and power dissipation of these devices. Analog neuromorphic computing promises to be a natural candidate for bringing intelligence to implantable neural interfaces, thus only needing to transmit sparse information gleaned from the raw neural recordings. Neuromorphic event-driven sampling can reduce datarate at the source producing spikes that can natively be processed by low-power, sparsely activated spiking neural networks (SNN), that detect events of interest such as epileptic seizures or occurrence of biological action potentials (AP). This work compares popular neuromorphic analog-spike converters (ASC) in terms of their robustness to interference and shows delta modulation to be superior to integrate and fire modes of spike generation. Further, a new type of delta modulation inspired by high threshold bursting neurons in the hippocampus is shown to extend the tradeoff between compression ratio and data fidelity for conventional delta modulation. Measured results from fabricated integrated circuits show excellent data compression rates far exceeding those of conventional analog digital converter with Nyquist sampling. Further, mixed-signal, clockless SNNs interfaced with this bursting ASC are shown to be able to classify the generated spikes to detect AP events with high accuracy while dissipating scant energy.

articles.title: An investigation on the Jacobi-Legendre polynomial expansion for potential-energy-surface fitting of multi-species triatomic systems
articles.abstract: In quantum-mechanical studies of few-atom systems the potential energy surface (PES) is usually formulated as an analytical function fitting a representative set of electronic energies computed at different nuclear geometries. While over the past decades several methods have been proposed for both the local and global fitting of three-atom PESs especially in the field of quantum reactive scattering, a new class of PES-fitting schemes has recently emerged in the neighbouring field of machine-learning force fields for molecular and materials science. In this work we focus on the Jacobi-Legendre polynomial (JLP) cluster-expansion approach, recently proposed by Domina et al. [Phys. Rev. B 108, 094102 (2023)] and tested on the modeling of different phases of (single-species) carbon systems. In particular, we set out to investigate to what extent a JLP-based approach can be used in PES fitting for quantum-mechanical studies of multi-species triatomic systems. To this purpose, we select two systems, HeLiH+ and HSO, that exhibit different topographical features in the respective PES. While, as expected, a pure JLP-based fitting scheme faces some difficulties in modeling the interaction at the long range, in the short and medium range a fairly good fit with RMSE of a few meV is obtained. A use case further confirming the accuracy of the fitted PES is provided through bound-state calculations on the HeLiH+ system.

articles.title: Cure State Estimation in Frontal Polymerization from Temperature Fields via Cascaded Inverse-Forward Deep Learning with Uncertainty Quantification
articles.abstract: Frontal polymerization (FP) is an emerging thermoset curing strategy that enables rapid, energy-efficient manufacturing of polymers and polymer composites through self-propagating exothermic polymerization fronts. The degree of cure, the primary determinant of mechanical properties, cannot be measured directly during processing, but the accompanying temperature field carries strong, well-defined features (notably the sharp gradients across the front) that can be acquired with reasonable accuracy in real time via infrared (IR) thermography. To date this thermal signal has been used mainly to track front kinematics rather than the underlying cure state, a task complicated by uncertainty in the initial degree of cure and the convection coefficient at boundaries. We address this gap with a cascaded deep learning pipeline: an inverse Stage 1 estimates these unknown but bounded initial and boundary conditions from the early-time temperature history, and a causal recurrent forward Stage 2 predicts the evolving cure field in real time from the temperature field, conditioned on the Stage 1 estimates. Trained on a finite-element dataset spanning the operating envelope, the pipeline attains low degree-of-cure root-mean-square error (RMSE): only 1.5× above the matched Stage 2 oracle given ground-truth conditions. A four-phase uncertainty quantification pipeline yields calibrated prediction intervals spanning ~1% of the cure range with 91% marginal coverage on a held-out test split. End-to-end inference runs in ≈0.1 s per trajectory on a single graphics processing unit (GPU). The framework is a simulation-validated prototype toward real-time, IR-driven process monitoring and digital-twin deployment, with experimental validation reserved for future work.

articles.title: Double-stranded RNA impairs epithelial barrier formation by redirecting airway basal cell differentiation
articles.abstract: Background Viral double-stranded RNA disrupts the airway epithelial barrier, but its specific impact on progenitor basal cells remains unknown. In this study, we stimulated undifferentiated normal human bronchial epithelial cells and VA10 cells, which function as basal cells, with the Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) ligand polycytidylic acid (poly I:C). The cells were subsequently cultured at an air-liquid interface (ALI) to evaluate airway epithelial barrier integrity and perform global gene expression analysis.Results Poly I:C stimulation significantly decreased trans-epithelial electrical resistance and reduced the expression of barrier-related genes. This barrier dysfunction was improved by silencing TLR3 or TIR-domain-containing adapter-inducing interferon-β. Transcriptomic analysis revealed a biphasic response to poly I:C. During the late phase, the transcriptional landscape shifted toward sustained inflammation and abnormal tissue remodeling. During the early phase, the transcriptomic profile suggests the initial prioritization of an antiviral state, which may affect essential epithelial differentiation and barrier genes.Conclusions Exposure of airway basal cells to double-stranded RNA triggered a TLR3/ TIR-domain-containing adapter-inducing interferon β-mediated biphasic response. An initial prioritization of antiviral defence compromises epithelial differentiation, which is followed by a late phase of unresolved chronic inflammation and abnormal remodeling. This cascade may provide a potential mechanistic explanation for how viral infections induce persistent airway barrier vulnerability and chronic dysfunction.

articles.title: The Affective Arena: Posthuman Subjectivity Beyond Cerebral Humanism
articles.title_zh: 情感竞技场：超越大脑人文主义的后人类主体性
articles.abstract: For four centuries, Western philosophy and psychology have prioritised reason over emotion, considering feelings to be private, secondary, and subordinate to rational thought. This article proposes the affective arena as a conceptual model of posthuman subjectivity that is relational, embodied, and materially entangled. The argument moves through three arenas. The first is the humanist arena, which follows the rationalist lineage from René Descartes to Immanuel Kant to twentieth-century cognitive psychology. Additionally, it puts into conversation the countertraditions of John Dewey, William James, David Hume, and Baruch Spinoza, who continuously brought affect and embodiment back to the core of subjectivity. The second is the deconstructive arena, which dismantles the coherence of the humanist subject. Michel Foucault, Jacques Derrida, Judith Butler, and Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak are the major intellectuals cited for structuring this argument. The problem with this model is that it offers only a partial account of the pre-reflective affective intensities that precede and exceed discursive inscription. The third is the posthuman affective arena, built from Sara Ahmed, Brian Massumi, and Karen Barad, and developed further through Rosi Braidotti, Teresa Brennan, and Patricia Clough. It addresses this gap by treating circulation, intensity, and entanglement as three irreducible dimensions of subject formation. For cultural psychology, this reframes memory, attention, learning, and development as affective material processes distributed across bodies, technologies, and social relations. The framework extends the discipline's methodological repertoire to include affective ethnography, biometric measurement, and network analysis, proposing a theoretically grounded and methodologically actionable model for studying subjectivity beyond the limits of the cognitive and discursive traditions that have long shaped the field.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文提出“情感竞技场”作为后人类主体性的概念模型，强调主体性具有关系性、具身性与物质纠缠性。文章依次讨论理性主义人文主义传统、解构主义对统一主体的拆解，以及以流通、强度和纠缠为核心的后人类情感理论。该框架将文化心理学中的记忆、注意、学习与发展重新理解为分布于身体、技术和社会关系中的情感性物质过程，并提出相应的方法论拓展。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 四个世纪以来，西方哲学与心理学一直将理性置于情感之上，认为情感是私人的、次要的，并且从属于理性思维。本文提出“情感竞技场”这一概念模型，用以理解具有关系性、具身性和物质纠缠性的后人类主体性。论证经由三个竞技场展开。第一个是人文主义竞技场，它沿循从勒内·笛卡尔到伊曼努尔·康德再到二十世纪认知心理学的理性主义谱系。同时，文章还使约翰·杜威、威廉·詹姆斯、大卫·休谟和巴鲁赫·斯宾诺莎的反传统彼此对话；这些思想家持续将情感与具身性带回主体性的核心位置。第二个是解构性竞技场，它瓦解了人文主义主体的连贯性。米歇尔·福柯、雅克·德里达、朱迪斯·巴特勒和加亚特里·查克拉沃蒂·斯皮瓦克是构建这一论证时援引的主要思想家。这一模型的问题在于，它只能部分说明先于并超出话语铭写的前反思性情感强度。第三个是后人类情感竞技场，它建立在萨拉·艾哈迈德、布赖恩·马苏米和凯伦·巴拉德的理论基础上，并经由罗西·布拉伊多蒂、特蕾莎·布伦南和帕特里夏·克拉夫的工作得到进一步发展。它通过将流通、强度和纠缠视为主体形成的三个不可约维度，弥补了这一缺口。对于文化心理学而言，这一视角将记忆、注意、学习和发展重新界定为分布于身体、技术和社会关系之中的情感性物质过程。该框架将学科的方法论工具扩展至情感民族志、生物测量和网络分析，并提出了一个具有理论基础且可在方法上实施的模型，用于研究超越长期塑造该领域的认知与话语传统局限的主体性。

articles.title: Operating-Condition-Decoupled Sparse Order-Domain Gear Fault Monitoring for Range-Extended Hybrid Agricultural Machinery in Hilly and Mountainous Areas
articles.title_zh: 面向丘陵山区增程式混合动力农业机械的工况解耦稀疏阶次域齿轮故障监测
articles.abstract: Vibration signals from range-extended hybrid agricultural machinery in hilly and mountainous areas are strongly nonstationary under variable conditions. Gear-fault components drift and broaden with rotational speed, causing normal fluctuations to overlap fault responses and increasing false alarms and missed detections. This study proposes a hybrid-condition-decoupled sparse order-domain monitoring (HCD-SOM) method. An operating-condition-powertrain-vibration simulation model and paired-sample strategy ensured that normal and fault samples shared identical slope, vehicle speed, load, battery state of charge (SOC), powertrain state, and speed trajectory, differing only in gear health. Variable-speed vibrations were transformed to the order domain; local amplitude, energy, and prominence features were sparsely selected before support vector machine classification. For 1000 normal and 1000 simulated fault samples, five random splits yielded a balanced accuracy of 0.9390 ± 0.0071, exceeding frequency-domain and decomposition-based filtering methods by 2.37 and 7.07 percentage points, respectively. Leave-one-level-out validation using mean speed, mean load, slope root mean square, and drive-shaft speed variability achieved 0.9354 across 12 unseen levels. Selected features were substantially more fault-sensitive than battery-, powertrain-, or mode-sensitive. The method suppresses operating-condition interference and improves fault-feature robustness under variable speed, supporting gear condition monitoring and maintenance decisions for hilly agricultural machinery.
articles.abstract_zh: 针对丘陵山区增程式混合动力农业机械在变工况下振动信号强非平稳、齿轮故障特征易漂移和展宽的问题，本文提出混合工况解耦稀疏阶次域监测方法（HCD-SOM）。该方法通过仿真模型和配对样本策略控制工况差异，将变速振动转入阶次域，并稀疏筛选局部幅值、能量和显著性特征后进行支持向量机分类。在模拟数据及未见工况等级验证中，该方法优于频域与基于分解的滤波方法，并提升了变速条件下齿轮故障特征的稳健性。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 丘陵和山区增程式混合动力农业机械的振动信号在变工况下具有很强的非平稳性。齿轮故障成分会随转速发生漂移和展宽，使正常波动与故障响应相互重叠，从而增加误报和漏检。本文提出一种混合工况解耦稀疏阶次域监测（HCD-SOM）方法。运行工况-动力传动系统-振动仿真模型和配对样本策略确保正常样本与故障样本具有完全相同的坡度、车速、负载、电池荷电状态（SOC）、动力传动系统状态和转速轨迹，仅在齿轮健康状态上存在差异。将变速振动转换至阶次域；在支持向量机分类之前，对局部幅值、能量和显著性特征进行稀疏选择。对于1000个正常样本和1000个模拟故障样本，五次随机划分得到的平衡准确率为0.9390±0.0071，分别比频域方法和基于分解的滤波方法高出2.37和7.07个百分点。使用平均速度、平均负载、坡度均方根和传动轴转速变异性开展的留一等级交叉验证，在12个未见等级上取得了0.9354的结果。所选特征对故障的敏感性显著高于其对电池、动力传动系统或运行模式的敏感性。该方法能够抑制工况干扰，并提高变速条件下故障特征的稳健性，为丘陵农业机械的齿轮状态监测和维护决策提供支持。

articles.title: PatternFormer: Learning Multiple Solution Patterns in Reaction--Diffusion Systems
articles.title_zh: PatternFormer：学习反应-扩散系统中的多重解模式
articles.abstract: Many nonlinear models across physics, chemistry, and biology exhibit multiple solutions for the same parameters, and capturing this entire solution set is essential for understanding pattern-forming systems. Yet existing learned surrogates are fundamentally single-valued: neural operators map each parameter to a single output, and physics-informed neural networks converge to one branch. We develop PatternFormer (PF), a large language model-based framework for learning the multiple solutions of nonlinear partial differential equations. By transforming unordered coexisting solutions into canonical sequences, PF produces structured solution sets in a single autoregressive pass, terminating automatically for finite families and enforcing physical residual constraints for unbounded ones. On nonlinear elliptic problems it recovers all solution branches in one inference step; on Gray--Scott it generates coexisting Turing patterns, including physically valid states absent from the reference data and beyond training. PF can also be sequentially fine-tuned across multistable systems, toward general foundation models for solution landscapes.
articles.abstract_zh: 许多非线性物理、化学和生物模型在相同参数下存在多个解，但现有学习代理模型通常只能输出单一解分支。本文提出基于大语言模型的PatternFormer框架，通过将无序共存解转化为规范序列，以一次自回归推理生成结构化解集。该方法在非线性椭圆问题和Gray-Scott系统中恢复或生成多种共存模式，并显示出跨多稳态系统顺序微调的潜力。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 物理、化学和生物学中的许多非线性模型在相同参数下呈现多个解，而捕获这一完整解集对于理解模式形成系统至关重要。然而，现有的学习代理模型在根本上是单值的：神经算子将每个参数映射为单一输出，而物理信息神经网络则收敛到一个分支。我们开发了PatternFormer（PF），这是一个基于大语言模型、用于学习非线性偏微分方程多重解的框架。通过将无序的共存解转换为规范序列，PF能够在单次自回归过程中生成结构化解集；对于有限解族可自动终止，而对于无界解族则施加物理残差约束。在非线性椭圆问题上，它能够在一次推理步骤中恢复所有解分支；在Gray-Scott系统上，它生成共存的图灵模式，其中包括参考数据中不存在且超出训练范围、但在物理上有效的状态。PF还可以在多稳态系统之间进行顺序微调，从而朝着用于解景观的通用基础模型发展。

articles.title: Allosteric β-Klotho Modulation to Restore FGF21 Sensitivity in Type 2 Diabetes
articles.title_zh: 通过β-Klotho变构调节恢复2型糖尿病中的FGF21敏感性
articles.abstract: Introduction: FGF21 resistance in type 2 diabetes (T2DM) limits the metabolic efficacy of endogenous FGF21 despite increased circulating concentrations, implicating impaired β-Klotho (KLB)–FGFR1c signaling as a therapeutically actionable mechanism. Objective:  To evaluate the structural, genetic, tissue-specific, and network-level rationale for allosteric KLB modulation as a strategy to restore FGF21 sensitivity in T2DM.  Methods:  A literature-grounded bioinformatics framework integrated Protein Data Bank structural curation, comparative structural analysis, characterization of the 39F7-defined allosteric site, KLB genetic-variant curation, tissue-specific receptor synthesis, interaction-network construction, and pharmacological feasibility assessment. Results No solved ternary FGF21–FGFR1c–KLB structure was identified. The homologous FGF23–FGFR1c–αKlotho complex was supported as a modeling template by low structural divergence between Klotho homologs. The KL1 Trp-295-centered site represented a noncompetitive activation interface, exemplified by the 39F7 antibody (KD = 86 pM). Five KLB variants were associated with body mass index, hepatic steatosis, or alcohol-related behavior. Tissue synthesis indicated adipose-predominant FGFR1c–KLB engagement for FGF21, whereas hepatic FGFR4–KLB signaling was comparatively weak. Network curation connected KLB with AMPK, SIRT1, PGC-1α, and mTOR, positioning KLB as a convergent structural node linking genetic susceptibility, tissue selectivity, and metabolic signaling.  Conclusion:  The integrated evidence supports KLB allosteric modulation as a mechanistically plausible approach to enhance endogenous FGF21 responsiveness and potentially overcome receptor-level resistance in T2DM, with particular relevance to adipose tissue, insulin sensitivity, energy expenditure, and cardiometabolic risk reduction in affected metabolic phenotypes. Experimental binding, cellular signaling, structural, pharmacokinetic, and in vivo studies are required to establish efficacy and tissue selectivity.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文评估了以β-Klotho（KLB）变构调节恢复2型糖尿病中FGF21敏感性的结构、生物遗传、组织特异性和网络层面依据。整合结构数据库、变异信息、组织受体表达及互作网络的分析表明，KLB可能是连接遗传易感性、组织选择性和代谢信号的关键节点。研究认为KLB变构调节具有增强内源性FGF21反应的机制合理性，但仍需开展结合、细胞、结构、药代和体内实验验证。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 引言：2型糖尿病（T2DM）中的FGF21抵抗限制了内源性FGF21的代谢效力，尽管其循环浓度升高，这提示β-Klotho（KLB）-FGFR1c信号受损是一种可通过治疗加以干预的机制。目的：评估将KLB变构调节作为恢复T2DM中FGF21敏感性策略的结构、生物遗传、组织特异性和网络层面依据。方法：一个以文献为基础的生物信息学框架整合了蛋白质数据库结构整理、比较结构分析、由39F7界定的变构位点表征、KLB遗传变异整理、组织特异性受体综合分析、相互作用网络构建和药理学可行性评估。结果：未发现已解析的FGF21-FGFR1c-KLB三元复合物结构。Klotho同源物之间较低的结构差异支持将同源的FGF23-FGFR1c-αKlotho复合物用作建模模板。以KL1 Trp-295为中心的位点代表一个非竞争性激活界面，39F7抗体即为例证，其KD为86 pM。五种KLB变异与体重指数、肝脂肪变性或酒精相关行为有关。组织综合分析显示，FGF21主要通过脂肪组织中的FGFR1c-KLB发挥作用，而肝脏FGFR4-KLB信号相对较弱。网络整理将KLB与AMPK、SIRT1、PGC-1α和mTOR相连接，使KLB成为连接遗传易感性、组织选择性和代谢信号的一个汇聚性结构节点。结论：整合证据支持将KLB变构调节视为一种在机制上合理的方法，可增强对内源性FGF21的反应性，并可能克服T2DM中的受体水平抵抗；该方法尤其与脂肪组织、胰岛素敏感性、能量消耗以及受影响代谢表型中心代谢风险降低相关。仍需开展实验性结合研究、细胞信号研究、结构研究、药代动力学研究和体内研究，以确立其疗效和组织选择性。

articles.title: Mobility-Aware Predictive Robust Secrecy Design for STAR-RIS-Assisted V2I Networks Under CSI Aging
articles.title_zh: CSI老化条件下STAR-RIS辅助车联网V2I网络的移动性感知预测鲁棒保密设计
articles.abstract: This paper investigates predictive robust physical-layer security (PLS) for a simultaneous transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS)-assisted downlink vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) network under mobility-induced channel aging. In high-mobility vehicular environments, the channel state information (CSI) available at the roadside transmitter becomes outdated due to Doppler effects and feedback delay, which can severely degrade secrecy performance in the presence of passive eavesdropping vehicles. To capture this practical impairment, we model the CSI aging through a Gauss--Markov time-correlation process and represent the residual prediction mismatch by norm-bounded uncertainty sets whose radii are linked to the channel time correlation. Based on the predicted CSI, we formulate a per-slot robust secrecy sum-rate (SSR) maximization problem by jointly optimizing the multiuser transmit beamforming (BF) and STAR-RIS transmission/reflection coefficients under the transmit-power budget and energy-splitting constraints. To solve the resulting non-convex and uncertainty-coupled problem, we develop a predictive robust alternating-optimization framework, where the BF subproblem is handled through S-procedure-based linear matrix inequalities and successive convex approximation, while the STAR-RIS coefficients are updated by feasibility-preserving projected steps. Numerical results show fast convergence and demonstrate that the proposed design outperforms non-predictive, non-robust, random STAR-RIS, and reflect-only RIS baselines, especially under high mobility, long CSI update intervals, and dense eavesdropping deployments.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文研究高速移动导致信道状态信息老化时，STAR-RIS辅助下行车联网基础设施通信的预测鲁棒物理层安全设计。研究以高斯-马尔可夫时间相关过程和范数有界不确定集建模CSI老化及预测失配，并联合优化多用户波束成形与STAR-RIS透射/反射系数，以最大化每时隙鲁棒保密和速率。数值结果表明，所提算法收敛迅速，并在高移动性、长CSI更新间隔及密集窃听车辆部署下优于多类基线方案。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 本文研究了在移动性引起的信道老化条件下，面向同时透射和反射可重构智能表面（STAR-RIS）辅助下行车对基础设施（V2I）网络的预测鲁棒物理层安全（PLS）。在高移动性车联网环境中，由于多普勒效应和反馈延迟，路侧发射机可获得的信道状态信息（CSI）会过时；在存在被动窃听车辆时，这会严重降低保密性能。为刻画这种实际损伤，我们通过高斯-马尔可夫时间相关过程建模CSI老化，并使用范数有界不确定集表示残余预测失配，且其半径与信道时间相关性相联系。基于预测CSI，我们构建了一个逐时隙鲁棒保密和速率（SSR）最大化问题，在发射功率预算和能量分配约束下联合优化多用户发射波束成形（BF）和STAR-RIS透射/反射系数。为解决由此产生的非凸且与不确定性耦合的问题，我们开发了一种预测鲁棒交替优化框架，其中，BF子问题通过基于S程序的线性矩阵不等式和逐次凸近似处理，而STAR-RIS系数则通过保持可行性的投影步骤更新。数值结果表明，该设计收敛迅速，并证明所提设计优于非预测、非鲁棒、随机STAR-RIS和仅反射RIS等基线方案，尤其是在高移动性、较长CSI更新间隔和密集窃听者部署条件下。

articles.title: Comparative Electromagnetic Performance of Dual-Stator/Rotor Flux- Switching PM Machines with Different Magnetization Patterns Considering Magnetic Saturation for Bearingless Applications
articles.title_zh: 考虑磁饱和的不同磁化模式双定子/转子磁通切换永磁电机电磁性能比较及其无轴承应用
articles.abstract: This paper presents an accurate analytical subdomain model to examine the electromagnetic performance of a dual-stator/rotor flux-switching permanent magnet (FSPM) machine, which is suitable for high-speed turbo machinery (compressors, blowers, turbines), energy storage systems (flywheels), and similar applications. Three different magnetization patterns are considered, namely tangential, radial, and Halbach arrays. Magnetic saturation is taken into account through a compensation technique that relies on the actual B-H curves of the iron laminations. The field solution is obtained by analytically solving Maxwell's equations and the saturation factors for both stator and rotor teeth are derived separately to calculate the air-gap flux density under nonlinear operating conditions. Using the proposed model, the local traction forces are compared across the three magnetization patterns for bearingless applications, and the air-gap flux density is computed and compared across all configurations under both linear and saturated states. The radial and tangential flux components, as well as the radial pressure, are thoroughly investigated. The validity of the analytical model is confirmed through comparisons with finite element analysis (FEA), demonstrating very good agreement.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文提出精确解析子域模型，用于研究适用于高速透平机械、飞轮等场景的双定子/转子磁通切换永磁电机。研究比较切向、径向和Halbach阵列三种磁化模式，并基于实际铁芯叠片B-H曲线补偿磁饱和效应。解析结果与有限元分析高度一致，且对无轴承应用中的局部牵引力、气隙磁密、磁场分量及径向压力进行了比较。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 本文提出了一种精确的解析子域模型，用于考察双定子/转子磁通切换永磁（FSPM）电机的电磁性能；该电机适用于高速透平机械，包括压缩机、鼓风机和涡轮机，亦适用于储能系统，包括飞轮，以及类似应用。研究考虑了三种不同的磁化模式，即切向、径向和Halbach阵列。通过一种依赖于铁芯叠片实际B-H曲线的补偿技术，考虑了磁饱和效应。通过解析求解麦克斯韦方程获得磁场解，并分别推导定子齿和转子齿的饱和系数，以计算非线性运行条件下的气隙磁通密度。利用所提出的模型，比较了三种磁化模式在无轴承应用中的局部牵引力，并计算和比较了所有构型在线性及饱和状态下的气隙磁通密度。对径向和切向磁通分量以及径向压力进行了深入研究。通过与有限元分析（FEA）进行比较，验证了该解析模型的有效性，结果显示二者符合得非常好。

articles.title: How Far Can a Single Vector Carry a Language? Mechanistic Limits of Inference-Time Steering for Low-Resource Devanagari Languages
articles.title_zh: 单一向量能承载多远的语言？面向低资源天城文语言的推理时引导机制极限
articles.abstract: Large multilingual decoder language models publish closed lists of supported languages: Llama 3.1 and Aya-23 both claim Hindi but not its lower-resource Devanagari sisters, Maithili, Nepali, and Bhojpuri. We ask a mechanistic question: where, and how far, can a single inference-time direction move such a model toward an unclaimed sister language, using only its Hindi representations and no fine-tuning, no new data, and no weight updates? Because the four languages share the Devanagari script and most subword tokens, anyshift mustreflect representation geometry rather than vocabulary. Across two architecturally distinct eight-billion-parameter decoders we report four findings. First, both models exhibit a shared hourglass geometry (languages distinct at the surface, merged mid network, and re-separated near the output), yet language identity is linearly decodable at every layer (about 99.5% accuracy). Second, adding the difference of per-language activation centroids at the re-divergence onset shifts generation toward the target (peak language adherence 4.03 of 5 for Nepali on Llama, scored by a three-judge cross-family panel) but only at the surface: fluency collapses into repetition, and no combination of model, target, and coefficient is simultaneously target-adherent and fluent. Third, few-shot prompting does reach fluent sisters, so the ceiling is a limit of single-direction steering, not model competence; steerability tracks linear separability, not proximity. Fourth, Hindi outperforms English as the steering source despite English’s pretraining dominance. Steering thus serves as a causal probe of where language identity is manipulable. We release a four-way parallel Devanagari corpus and an evaluation harness.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文考察单一推理时激活方向能否在无需微调、额外数据或权重更新的前提下，将多语种大语言模型从印地语引导至迈蒂利语、尼泊尔语和博杰普尔语等低资源天城文语言。实验发现，语言表征在网络中呈现表层分离、中层汇合、输出前再分离的共同结构，且各层语言身份均可被高精度线性解码。单向量引导可提升目标语言符合度，却导致流畅性退化；少样本提示可生成流畅文本，表明瓶颈在于单方向引导的能力边界而非模型本身的语言能力。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 大型多语种解码语言模型会公布其支持语言的封闭列表：Llama 3.1和Aya-23都声称支持印地语，却不包括其低资源的天城文姐妹语言迈蒂利语、尼泊尔语和博杰普尔语。我们提出一个机制性问题：仅利用模型的印地语表征，且不进行微调、不加入新数据、不更新权重时，单一推理时方向能够在何处、又能在多大程度上将此类模型推向一种未被宣称支持的姐妹语言？由于这四种语言共享天城文字母和大多数子词标记，任何转变都必须反映表征几何，而非词汇差异。我们在两个架构不同的80亿参数解码器上报告了四项发现。第一，两个模型都呈现共同的沙漏形几何结构，即语言在表层彼此不同，在网络中部合并，并在接近输出端时再次分离；然而，语言身份在每一层都可被线性解码，准确率约为99.5%。第二，在再分离开始处加入各语言激活中心点之差，会使生成向目标语言偏移，例如Llama上的尼泊尔语峰值语言符合度达到5分制中的4.03分，该结果由一个跨语系的三位评审小组评分，但这一效果仅停留在表层：流畅性会退化为重复，且不存在任何模型、目标语言和系数组合能够同时实现目标语言符合度和流畅性。第三，少样本提示确实能够生成流畅的姐妹语言，因此这一上限是单方向引导的限制，而非模型能力的限制；可引导性与线性可分性相关，而不与语言接近性相关。第四，尽管英语在预训练中占主导地位，印地语作为引导源仍优于英语。因此，引导可作为一种因果探针，用于揭示语言身份在何处可以被操控。我们发布了一个四语平行天城文语料库和一个评估工具框架。

In this work, we advance the field by introducing the concept of surface altermagnetism (SAM), wherein altermagnetic spin polarization emerges at the surfaces of collinear antife… [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116705] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026
articles.abstract_zh: 该工作围绕“表面交错磁性”概念展开，旨在将交错磁性研究从磁性材料的体相自旋极化电子态拓展至表面现象。根据所提供的摘要片段，作者关注共线反铁磁材料表面出现的交错磁性自旋极化；具体理论、材料体系与结论需查阅原文。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 作者：Yuzhong Hu、Pan Zhou、Baoru Pan、Songmin Liu、Binchang Zhou和Lizhong Sun。迄今为止，对交错磁性的研究主要聚焦于磁性材料中具有自旋极化的体相电子态。在本工作中，我们通过引入表面交错磁性（SAM）的概念推进该领域；在这一概念中，交错磁性自旋极化出现在共线反铁磁……的表面。所提供摘要在此处截断，关于具体机制、研究对象和结论的完整信息需查阅原文。
articles.focus_summary: 该工作提出表面交替磁性概念，指出共线反铁磁材料的表面可以产生交替磁性自旋极化。研究将交替磁性的关注点从体相自旋极化电子态扩展到表面电子结构和表面磁性现象。
articles.focus_relation: 与团队的交替磁性、磁性拓扑性质、电子结构计算和自旋电子学方向直接相关。表面诱导的自旋极化为利用对称性、界面和表面终止调控纯自旋响应提供了新切入点。
articles.focus_suggestion: 建议分析该机制所需的磁空间群与表面对称性条件，并采用第一性原理和Wannier模型计算表面谱函数、自旋纹理及输运信号。可进一步研究缺陷、吸附、应变和异质结对表面交替磁性的稳定性与可探测性的影响。

By fabricating the resonator directly on yttrium iron garnet thin films grown on rare-earth-free Y₃Sc₂Ga_{… [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116706] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026

articles.title: Ultrathin AAO-Confined Pulsed Electrodeposition of Ordered Ag Nanocolumn Arrays as Sensitive and Uniform SERS Substrates
articles.abstract: Ultrathin anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) templates provide a promising route for constructing ordered plasmonic nanoarrays, but their application in SERS substrates is often limited by insufficient template–substrate contact and nonuniform pore filling during electrodeposition. Herein, we apply ultrathin AAO template-assisted confined electrodeposition to fabricate ordered Ag nanocolumn arrays for SERS substrates. Surface modification was introduced to improve the wettability and interfacial contact between the AAO template and the Au-coated substrate, thereby maintaining template stability during electrodeposition and suppressing uncontrolled Ag growth outside the confined nanochannels. By further regulating the pulsed electrodeposition potential, uniform Ag nanocolumn growth within the AAO nanochannels was achieved. The optimized Ag nanocolumn array substrate exhibited a limit of detection of 10–10 M for Rhodamine 6G, an enhancement factor up to 10⁸, and a point-to-point relative standard deviation of 7.03%. This work provides a practical strategy for constructing structurally uniform ordered nanocolumn arrays with stable SERS responses.

articles.title: Aero-engine RUL Prediction Method Based on Deep Equilibrium Network with Degradation Alignment and Domain Adaptation
articles.abstract: Aiming at the problems of domain distribution shift, gradient vanishing, and insufficient generalization performance in aero-engine remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, this paper constructs DAI-DEQ and adaptive DAI-DEQ models by integrating degradation alignment, deep equilibrium structure, and adaptive modules, and proposes a novel aero-engine RUL prediction method based on a deep equilibrium network with collaborative degradation alignment and domain adaptation. First, multi-working condition clustering normalization, exponential moving average smoothing, and random forest feature selection are applied to preprocess the NASA C-MAPSS dataset. The Degradation Alignment Indicator (DAI) is embedded as an attention weighting coefficient into the deep equilibrium network built upon Anderson fixed-point iteration, which alleviates gradient vanishing and strengthens the extraction of degradation features. By combining the gradient reversal layer and domain discriminator, domain adaptation is realized, and Bayesian neural networks with Monte Carlo sampling are introduced to quantify prediction uncertainty. Experimental results show that in intra-domain prediction on the four standard C-MAPSS subsets, the RMSE values of the DA-DEQ model are 7.50 (FD001), 7.35 (FD002), 8.42 (FD003), and 7.41 (FD004), outperforming existing mainstream methods, including IDMFFN and GA-Transformer. In cross-domain transfer experiments, the RMSE of the adaptive DA-DEQ model drops from 49.85 to 12.90 (a decline of 74.1%) under the FD001→FD002 scenario, effectively alleviating domain shift. Ablation experiments confirm that removing the DAI module increases the maximum RMSE by up to 4.56 on FD002 and FD004, verifying its core effect. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves remarkable superiority in prediction accuracy, training stability, and generalization ability, and holds significant practical value for aero-engine health prognosis.

articles.title: Distinguishability Transitions from Global Quantum Snapshots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum states generated by generic time evolution are locally featureless: local measurements return random outcomes that are identical for all states. However, global snapshots in the computational basis are surprisingly effective at distinguishing between quantum states. We explore the ability of Bayesian classifiers to discriminate between many random quantum states using a small number of measurement outcomes. We identify a phase transition in the ability of the classifier to distinguish between k candidate states with m shots controlled by the variable x = m / ln k, and derive the threshold value x_c. We extend our results to low-depth circuits near the onset of anti-concentration, as well as to noisy circuits and phase-random states.

articles.title: Transient and universal regimes in quantum reaction-transport kinetics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum reaction-transport systems consist of coherently propagating particles that irreversibly react upon encounter. Their relaxation is commonly classified as reaction-limited or transport-limited, depending on the relative timescales of reaction and particle transport. We show that this expectation fails in low dimensions by studying the quantum binary annihilation, A+A → emptyset, where reaction processes acquire singular fluctuation corrections below the upper critical dimension D_c=2. Consequently, fluctuations dominate the asymptotic kinetics for D<2. In one dimension, they render mean-field relaxation transient and drive the system toward a transport-limited regime with nsim t⁻¹/², governed by a quantum-Zeno scale even for arbitrarily weak loss. At D=2, the kinetics acquires logarithmic corrections, whereas above two dimensions mean-field scaling is asymptotically restored. At and below the upper critical dimension, mean-field behavior can nevertheless persist over parametrically long crossover times before the asymptotic fluctuation-dominated regime emerges. We also show that the same fluctuations generate effective elastic collisions despite the absence of microscopic coherent interactions. In D>1, these collisions redistribute momentum populations and are parametrically faster than losses in the transport-limited regime, allowing the system to approach a quasi-stationary thermal state.

articles.title: Implicit size dependence of the valence electron concentration criterion in high-entropy alloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The valence electron concentration (VEC) is the most widely used predictor of FCC against BCC stability in high-entropy alloys (HEAs), yet it is a compositional average carrying no information about atomic size. Using the macroscopic atom model, we show that the mixing enthalpy is almost size-blind, shifting by less than 6% even when constituent volumes differ by a factor of 2, so that size can act only on the electron count. That action equals exactly the covariance of the atomic surface V²/³ with the valence electron count, divided by its mean. This covariance is not free. Volume and valence are strongly anti-correlated across the elements used to build HEAs, so the size-corrected count is an affine rescaling of VEC over 265 characterized alloys and improves no prediction. VEC already encodes atomic size, which explains its success and locates its failure among large, electron-rich elements. Chemistry sets the enthalpy through one switch element.

articles.title: Non-Hermitian topology in driven-dissipative systems: correspondence with quantum correlations and a resource for entanglement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Directional amplification, in which signals are amplified selectively depending on their propagation direction, is a key resource for quantum information processing and stands in one-to-one correspondence with non-trivial non-Hermitian topology. So far, this correspondence has concerned the mean fields, and thus classical response. Here we turn to the quantum fluctuations, giving access to correlations and entanglement. For phase-preserving amplifiers, we derive analytic expressions for the normal and anomalous correlations, showing that non-trivial topology produces correlations that grow exponentially with the distance between modes and approach the largest values compatible with the uncertainty relations. The associated correlation length diverges at the topological phase transition. Entanglement nonetheless remains local, set by the competition between normalised anomalous correlations and the asymmetry of the mode occupations. For the bosonic Kitaev chain, a phase-sensitive amplifier, the system instead splits into two halves that are internally fully correlated yet mutually uncorrelated. Our work prepares the ground for exploring the quantum properties of non-Hermitian topological systems with state-of-the-art platforms such as cavity optomechanics and superconducting circuits.

articles.title: Phase stability and mechanical response of Ag-interlayered Al/Cu resistance spot-welded joints
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dissimilar Al/Cu joints are essential to battery-pack assemblies; however, their mechanical strength is limited by brittle Al-Cu intermetallic compounds (IMCs) such as Al2Cu and Al4Cu9. Interlayer strategies to suppress these phases remain largely empirical, lacking a predictive framework linking interlayer chemistry to the phases that form and to their intrinsic mechanical character. Here an Ag interlayer is introduced and combines computational thermodynamics, first-principles calculations, microstructural characterization, and mechanical testing into a single self-consistent description of the joint. CALculation of PHAse Diagrams (CALPHAD) equilibrium and Scheil simulations predict the solidification path of the Al-rich Al-Ag fusion zone and explain why Cu incorporation is limited when Ag is present; energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) confirm an FCC Al-Ag solid solution as the dominant constituent. First-principles phonon calculations within the quasiharmonic approximation yield finite-temperature entropy and Gibbs energy, benchmarked against CALPHAD, while elastic constants assess ductility via the Pugh criterion (i.e., the bulk/shear (B/G) modulus ratio). All Al-Ag phases, including the observed solid solution, exceed the Pugh threshold of 1.75, whereas the targeted Al-Cu IMCs do not, giving a mechanistic basis for the interlayer's effectiveness. This microstructural change translates into improved performance: nominal strength rises from 47.9 to 67.4 MPa. Nanoindentation gives a fusion-zone reduced modulus of 82.8 GPa (Young's modulus 82.0 GPa), versus a calculated 0 K Voigt-Reuss-Hill value of 71.4 GPa. The present work establishes a transferable CALPHAD, first-principles, and experiment workflow for rational interlayer selection in dissimilar-metal joining.

articles.title: Emergent Electronic Bond-Order Wave in a Quasi-One-Dimensional Chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collective order is notoriously difficult to stabilize in one dimension, where strong fluctuations suppress symmetry-breaking states. Here we report the emergence of an electronic bond-order wave (BOW) in the quasi-one-dimensional (1D) material Ba9Rh8O24, in which structural bonds become active electronic degrees of freedom that overcome 1D fluctuations to establish long-range order. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction uncovers a striking inversion of inequivalent Rh-Rh bonds across a transition TA = 180 K, where short and long bonds interchange their identities rather than undergoing conventional Peierls dimerization. This bond inversion coincides with a heat-capacity anomaly and a profound reorganization of the dielectric response with strong suppression of dielectric loss upon cooling. The BOW exhibits strongly nonlinear, frequency-dependent I-V characteristics, clockwise hysteresis, and nonvolatile memristive switching. These findings uncover an unprecedented transformation from a dynamic bond liquid to a rigid yet electrically reconfigurable BOW, establishing bond-centered electronic order as a new organizing principle for 1D quantum matter.

articles.title: Quantum Phase Transitions and Fractional Quantized Anomalous Hall Insulators in Rhombohedral Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (FQAHE) has been discovered in twisted MoTe₂ and rhombohedral graphene/hBN moiré superlattices. Such van der Waals heterostructures feature a tuning knob of gate displacement field D, which is absent from the conventional fractional quantum Hall systems in two-dimensional electron gases. D plays a critical role in engineering FQAHE and other emergent quantum states and provides an exciting new opportunity to explore their quantum phase transitions. However, the microscopic details of such transitions and temperature-dependent transport have remained mostly elusive. Here we report systematic resistance measurements in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene/hBN moiré superlattices. We found that the displacement field-driven phase transitions between Composite Fermi liquid, Fermi liquid, Fractional Chern insulators, and insulating states are described by semi-circle relations of the longitudinal and transverse resistivities (or conductivities), largely unexplored in the fractional quantum Hall systems. This agrees with a spatially separated two-phase picture for the phase transitions and further indicates a new insulator phase--fractional quantized anomalous Hall insulator. By comparing the temperature-dependence of longitudinal resistance with the thermal activation model, we estimated the transport gap sizes in three fractional Chern insulator states. Our work shed light on the quantum and temperature evolutions of fractional Chern insulator states--providing necessary background for anyon-braiding and gate-defined junctions in rhombohedral graphene.

articles.title: Origin of Flat Bands and Role of Electron Correlation in Lutetium Hydrides
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lutetium hydrides (LuHₓ, 1.75 ≤ x ≤ 3) form a diverse series of phases, several of which superconduct under pressure. Characterizing their electronic properties has remained challenging owing to a high propensity for hydrogen defect formation, and recent angle-resolved photoemission (ARPES) measurements reveal puzzling flat-band regions that position these materials as candidates where superconductivity and flat-band physics may intersect. Here, by combining density functional theory, dynamical mean-field theory, and the constrained random-phase approximation, we uncover the microscopic origin and correlation nature of these flat bands. Across all compositions, the screened on-site Coulomb interaction is larger for H-s states than for Lu-d states due to compact hydrogen orbitals. Nevertheless, these systems remain weakly correlated metals: the nearly filled H-s shell admits little charge fluctuation, so its large interaction acts as a static level shift rather than a source of correlation. Although hydrogen primarily occupies tetrahedral sites at x=2, we discover that anti-site defects--where hydrogens occupy slightly unfavorable octahedral sites--generate both the ARPES flat-band features and the low-energy optical absorption peak, attesting to the usual defective nature of such materials in experimental samples. We further find that correlation strength is governed primarily by hydrogen orbital filling at these sites rather than the interaction magnitude itself. Consequently, we identify hydrogen orbital filling as the fundamental organizing principle dictating correlation and low-energy flat-band physics in lutetium hydrides.

articles.title: Prethermal ripplons in quenched binary Bose-Einstein condensates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prethermal states--long-lived quasi-equilibrium configurations--occur in a wide range of physical systems that exhibit fast dephasing or reconfiguration followed by slow relaxation towards thermal equilibrium. We experimentally studied the 1D interface between immiscible 2D Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs); following a quench, the interfacial capillary waves (ripplons) quickly relaxed into a long-lived prethermal state characterized by a persistent non-equipartition of energy, evoking the classic Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou problem. We directly measured the interface's height profile as it evolved in time, identified the contribution of individual ripplon modes, and find that, though their individual amplitudes are thermally distributed, they are not in thermal equilibrium--high-momentum modes rapidly equilibrated with the bulk phonon modes of the 2D BEC, while lower momentum modes remained at elevated temperatures, forming a long-lived prethermal configuration for the whole system. We attribute this to kinematic isolation: the absence of energy- and momentum-conserving relaxation processes in our system at ultracold temperature.

articles.title: High-pressure elastic properties of GeO2 polymorphs up to 120 GPa
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We systematically investigated the phase stability and pressure dependence of the elastic properties of four GeO2 polymorphs: rutile-, CaCl2-, alpha-PbO2-, and pyrite-type phases using theoretical calculations based on density functional theory. The elastic constants were calculated at 5 GPa intervals within the respective stability ranges of the four phases, as determined from static enthalpy calculations. We further employed a classical strain-coupled Landau free-energy expansion to describe the pressure evolution of the elastic response associated with the rutile- to CaCl2-type transition and to elucidate the origin of the elastic softening near the transition. The rutile- to CaCl2-type phase transition is consistent with a Landau-type second-order transition, with a critical pressure of 14.6 GPa obtained from the strain-based analysis. As the transition pressure approaches, elastic softening develops in the rutile-type phase, resulting in anomalous pressure dependence of the bulk and shear modulus. The calculated elastic-wave anisotropy increases markedly near the transition, primarily due to the rapid reduction in shear-wave velocity, reaching a maximum of approximately 122% at 22.5 GPa. Following the transition, the anisotropy decreases sharply in the CaCl2-type phase and exhibits a discontinuity at the CaCl2-type/alpha-PbO2 -type phase boundary. The higher-pressure alpha-PbO2- and pyrite-type phases exhibit comparatively weak pressure dependence of anisotropy, with a small discontinuity at their respective phase transition boundaries. The pyrite-type phase has the lowest anisotropy, reaching only approximately 4-5% at high pressure, consistent with the high-symmetry cubic structure and nearly isotropic elastic-wave propagation.

articles.title: Intrinsic (valley) thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in graphene for integer quantum Hall phases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the intrinsic contribution to the (valley) thermal Hall conductivity of phonons in (Semenoff-gapped) graphene in the quantum Hall regime where bulk electron thermal transport is suppressed. The (valley) thermal Hall transport of phonons considered here originates from a phonon (valley) Hall viscosity induced by electron (valley) Hall conductivity and viscosity via geometric electron-phonon coupling. The so generated phonon (valley) Hall viscosity is identified with the emergent (valley) Hall viscosity recently introduced in Phys. Lett. A 595, 132096 (2026). While our calculations refer to graphene, they may very well be generalized to other Dirac materials like group-VI transition metal dichalcogenides. We discuss the prospect of measuring the phonon thermal Hall conductivity in graphene-based heterostructures and estimate the corresponding valley response induced by electrons in the inversion symmetry broken phase.

articles.title: The Role of Concentration in Determining NaCl Nucleation Mechanism: A Story of Pathways Coexistence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deciphering the microscopic details of crystal nucleation remains a key open problem in chemical physics. For aqueous sodium chloride (NaCl), the extent to which nucleation involves amorphous ion aggregation, and the supersaturation regime in which two-step-like behavior emerges, remains actively debated. In this work, we examine NaCl nucleation at 12, 13, and 14 mol/kg (S = 3.2, 3.5, 3.8) using unbiased path sampling with inftyRETIS. Through a combination of reaction coordinate analysis, joint and conditional probability distributions, diffusion tensor analysis, and conditional free energy landscapes, we identify nucleation pathways without a priori mechanistic assumptions. While all concentrations are governed by the same reaction coordinate, indicating that nucleus growth and structural ordering are central to crossing the barrier, the nature of reactive trajectories changes with supersaturation. At lower concentrations, nucleation mainly occurs via tightly coupled increases in cluster size and ordering, compatible with a one-step-like mechanism. As concentration increases, amorphous aggregation becomes increasingly decoupled from crystallization, and pathways involving substantial amorphous growth prior to crystallization become progressively more probable. Importantly, these pathways coexist within a single broad reaction channel rather than proceeding through distinct metastable intermediate states. Together, these results reconcile earlier, contradictory reports on NaCl nucleation mechanisms and support a view of nucleation as an ensemble of competing reactive pathways whose relative probabilities vary continuously with supersaturation. More broadly, our findings illustrate that substantial mechanistic diversity can emerge within a classical nucleation framework, without requiring distinct non-classical descriptions.

articles.title: Comprehensive molecular dynamics study of the dynamical properties of a dense binary hard-sphere mixture
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an extensive molecular dynamics (MD) study of the dynamical properties of a binary hard-sphere fluid over a wide range of packing fractions, φ approx 0.357-0.582. The self-diffusivity, D, and shear viscosity, η, are computed using an efficient implementation of the Einstein--Helfand method. The finite-size effects in D scale as 1/N^α, with α increasing from approximately 1/3 to 3/4 with increasing φ, whereas those in η are negligible except for φ gtrsim 0.554, where they scale as 1/N. The data are then extrapolated to the thermodynamic limit to obtain Dᵢₙfₜy and ηᵢₙfₜy. Both coefficients show a super-Arrhenius dependence on φ for dense states, accompanied by a breakdown of the Stokes--Einstein relation. Although both Dᵢₙfₜy(φ) and ηᵢₙfₜy(φ) data are well described by an exponential form, we demonstrate that these fits do not provide reliable estimates of the critical packing fraction, φ₀, owing to the substantial extrapolation required beyond the accessible equilibrium range. We find the commonly assumed proportionality between η and the structural relaxation time, τ_α , to not hold for this system. For φgtrsim 0.570, the van Hove self-correlation function Gₛ(r, τ) exhibits a spatial exponential decay at intermediate times, τ, signaling dynamic heterogeneity. The characteristic decay length scales as λ sim τ^ν, with ν approx 1/3, in contrast to the conventional square-root scaling. We also investigate temporal heterogeneity through the four-point dynamic susceptibility, χ₄(τ), and its peak time, τ₄. These findings provide rigorous benchmark MD data for computational studies of glassy dynamics and establish a reference for testing theoretical models in dense disordered systems.

articles.title: Composition and Surface Termination Control Band Alignments in P3HT/Perovskite Heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite heterostructures are emerging platforms for energy conversion and optoelectronic devices, yet the effects of composition and surface terminations on band alignment remain poorly understood. Here, using high-throughput first-principles calculations, we systematically reveal the effect of composition and surface termination on the band alignment of 820 heterostructures formed between poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) variants and conventional and mixed-cation metal halide perovskites. Band edge analysis predicts concentration dependent band alignments, with most Pb and Sn based perovskites exhibiting Type II and III behavior while mixed-cation CsMASnBr3 uniquely forms Type-I junctions with all P3HT variants. Explicit interface calculations reveal that surface termination can reverse the predicted alignment in conventional tin perovskites, while the mixed cation perovskite preserves Type-I alignment with P3HT regardless of termination. Despite negligible charge transfer, termination dependent band offsets produce markedly different carrier confinement, establishing design principles for engineering P3HT/perovskite interfaces.
articles.focus_summary: 该工作通过高通量第一性原理计算研究P3HT变体与金属卤化物钙钛矿构成的820种异质结构，系统分析组分和表面终止对能带对齐的影响。结果表明，多数铅基和锡基钙钛矿表现为II型或III型能带对齐，而混合阳离子CsMASnBr3与各P3HT变体均形成I型结；显式界面计算还显示表面终止可改变部分体系的预测对齐类型。
articles.focus_relation: 与团队的卤化物钙钛矿、光电能源材料、异质结构界面、电荷转移和高通量筛选方向高度相关。其从体相能带推断到显式界面验证的流程，对界面光伏材料设计具有直接借鉴价值。
articles.focus_suggestion: 建议跟进其界面模型、带边校正和表面终止处理方法，并结合GW-BSE、非绝热分子动力学研究激子解离、载流子注入及非辐射复合。可将筛选框架扩展到动态缺陷、离子迁移和稳定性约束。

articles.title: The validity of the Stokes-Einstein relation in ionic liquids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) exhibit supercooled liquids behavior even above room temperature and the Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation is often considered to be invalid in ILs as that in supercooled liquids. However, the conclusion is usually drawn based on some variants of SE relation. In this work, we have systematically investigated the validity of the Stokes-Einstein relation in ILs by performing molecular dynamics simulations of coarse-grained IL within the temperature range of 400-800 K. Both the original SE formulation, and two commonly employed variants, were examined to assess their applicability and consistency. These three formulas yield distinctly different results, indicating that the two variants are not reliable substitutes for the original SE relation. The inconsistency suggests the fact that the r in Stokes law varies with conditions. The breakdown arises from the ion correlations introduced by the strong electrostatic interactions. This proposition is further confirmed by simulations.

articles.title: An encoded asymmetric ligand for metal-selective topological assembly of two-dimensional metal-organic frameworks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional metal-organic frameworks (2D MOFs), with diverse topological architectures, provide a powerful platform for exploring unconventional electronic and lattice-dynamical responses. Yet their structural diversity remains fundamentally constrained by the fixed geometry of high-symmetry ligands. Here, we introduce an encoded asymmetric ligand, benzo[b]triphenylene-2,3,6,7,11,12-hexaol (BTH), for metal-selective topological assembly. By integrating multi-site coordination fields with sterically differentiated environments, BTH exhibits distinct topological programmability: different divalent metal ions direct divergent framework architectures. Specifically, coordination of BTH with divalent Cu(II) and Zn(II) ions assembles Cu-BTH-MOF with a dual-mode hexagonal pore topology and Zn-BTH-MOF with uniform hexagonal channels, respectively, as supported by PXRD Pawley refinement, structural simulations, and pore-size distribution analysis. Furthermore, this topological divergence is accompanied by a significant divergence in charge-transport properties, with Cu-BTH-MOF reaching an electrical conductivity of 1.186 x 10-3 S cm-1, more than six orders of magnitude higher than that of Zn-BTH-MOF (3.38 x 10-10 S cm-1). This work establishes ligand desymmetrization as a programmable strategy for metal-selective topological diversification in 2D MOFs.

articles.title: Heteroepitaxial Growth of PbSe on InP Substrates via Lattice-Matched III-V Buffer Layers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detector cost remains a barrier to the widespread adoption of mid-wave infrared (3-5 micron) technology. PbSe, an inexpensive narrow band gap IV-VI semiconductor that has been used since the early 1940s, delivers high performance for infrared detection despite the abundance of grain boundaries in polycrystalline films. Epitaxial growth, however, could provide superior crystalline quality and interfaces, but suitable substrates remain limited for PbSe. Recent PbSe heteroepitaxy has focused primarily on III-V, II-VI and group-IV substrates that each offer a comparatively narrow range of lattice-matched alloys for heterostructure engineering. Here we show that InP-based heteroepitaxy provides access to a broader materials platform while limiting the lattice mismatch with PbSe to approximately 4%. We grow 150-nm thick PbSe films by molecular beam epitaxy on 200-nm thick In0.53Ga0.47As and In0.52Al0.48As buffers on (001) InP substrates. Reflection high-energy electron diffraction and X-ray diffraction show (001)-oriented rock-salt PbSe with an out-of-plane lattice constant of 6.12 Angstrom on both buffers. Photoluminescence (PL) is observed from room-temperature down to 12 K and the peak wavelength red-shifts from 3.7 to 5.0 microns. Under identical measurement conditions, the room-temperature peak PL intensities from films on In0.53Ga0.47As and In0.52Al0.48As are approximately 1.9x and 1.3x that of a PbSe on GaAs substrate reference, respectively. These results establish an InP-compatible platform for integrating narrow band-gap PbSe with a broad range of ternary and quaternary III-V alloys, including, for example, structures in which In0.53Ga0.47As serves as both a short-wave infrared absorber and a template for PbSe growth.

articles.title: Twist and strain identification in moiré heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The geometrical and electronic properties of moiré materials are highly sensitive to the twist and strain in the samples due to the moiré magnifying effect. Accurate identification of twist and strain in moiré materials is therefore essential. In this work, we establish a general framework to extract the twist and strain configurations from moiré images with either atomic or moiré scale resolution. With only moiré-wavelength information, we show that there is a continuous family of possible twist and strain configurations, each one accounting for different orientations of the moiré pattern. To estimate the most likely twist-strain configuration, we discuss additional constraints and methods involving the minimum elastic energy and the electronic spectra. The minimum elastic energy, in particular, reflects that shear configurations become much more favorable as the strain increases. As an example of the developed methodology, we discuss the formation and identification of strained triangular moiré patterns. Our framework provides a comprehensive approach to identify the twist and strain configurations in systems with moiré-scale resolution.

articles.title: Eight-unit-cell electronic modulations in cuprates originating from local molecular orbitals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pair density wave (PDW) state with eight-unit-cell (8a0) periodicity has been widely regarded as the primary order in cuprates, yet its existence and origin remain subjects of intense debate. Using spectroscopic imaging scanning tunneling microscopy, we observe spatial modulations of the electronic states with approximately 8a0 periodicity in both the superconducting and insulating regimes of hole-doped Ca2CuO2Cl2 cuprate. We find that the 8a0 spatial patterns are generated by the formation of molecular orbitals by doped holes, which organize into 4a0*4a0 plaquettes as the basic unit. Our results identify the 4a0 molecular orbital as the fundamental electronic building block in cuprates, while the 8a0 PDW represents a spatial subharmonic that emerges at sufficiently high doping.

articles.title: Geodesic Trapping and Escape of Active Particles on Curved Surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active particles on curved surfaces can become trapped along closed geodesics even without physical barriers. We show that escape from these geometric traps exposes a fundamental distinction between continuous and discrete reorientation. At high Péclet numbers, active Brownian particles escape efficiently through rotational diffusion, whereas run-and-tumble particles remain trapped much longer; at low Péclet numbers, both reduce to passive diffusion. Gaussian curvature controls escape by focusing or defocusing neighboring geodesics, producing distinct asymptotic scalings of the mean exit time.

articles.title: A discrete Stiefel-Whitney invariant with twofold rotation symmetry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review Stiefel--Whitney invariants and give a discrete formulation of an additional Z₂ invariant for two-dimensional spinful insulators with twofold rotation and time-reversal symmetries (layer group p1121'). A singular gauge transformation specifies a real bundle over the quotient of the Brillouin torus, whose second Stiefel--Whitney number defines the invariant. We derive its dependence on the choice of auxiliary gauge function and prove invariance under changes of Bloch frame and additivity under direct sums. The discrete formula uses overlaps of independently chosen Bloch frames and symmetry-compatible Pin₊ lifts on the boundary of a half Brillouin zone. Atomic and topological-insulator models illustrate the formula and distinguish the additional invariant from the Kane--Mele index. Together with three quantized Z₂ partial polarizations and the filling number, it labels the known stable classification ZoplusZ₂oplus ⁴.

articles.title: Fractional Chern Insulators in Twisted Bilayer Optical Lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisted bilayer materials provide a versatile platform for realizing novel topological states. Motivated by recent experimental realization of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates in twisted bilayer optical lattices, we theoretically investigate topological states for cold atoms trapped in such a system. At single-particle level, the system hosts nearly flat moiré bands under appropriate experimental parameters. Although these noninteracting bands are topologically trivial in the Altland-Zirnbauer classification, we find that atomic interactions can induce a flat Chern band based on self-consistent Hartree-Fock calculations. Furthermore, exact diagonalization identifies a fractional Chern insulator phase at fractional filling. Our work thus paves the way for exploring strongly correlated topological phases in highly tunable twisted bilayer optical lattices.

articles.title: Morphology and depletion force-based large-scale self-assembly of nanocubes on surface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-assembling nanoparticles is a highly efficient and facile way to form functional nano-, micro- and macrostructures. However, currently available methods lack precision and controllability in size, shape and composition, suffer from poor reproducibility and scalability, and require complex steps and expensive materials. Here, we present the uniform morphology-induced and depletion force-directed nanoparticle assembly on surface (MIDAS) method with gold nanocubes (AuNCs). Using this approach, morphology-sensitive depletion forces trigger shape-selective flocculation and assembly of the AuNCs with uniform size and shape. Importantly, the surface roughness-controlled substrate drives the large-scale formation of AuNC-assembled monolayers (2D AuNAMs) or three-dimensional AuNC-assembled multilayers (3D AuNAMs) in a highly specific manner without any complex ligand modification or preparation steps. Lattice-gas modeling and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations show the depletion force is the key parameter determining supercrystal morphology and corroborate the experimental findings. This work establishes a generalizable nanoparticle assembly mechanism and demonstrates the broad applicability of the MIDAS strategy for scalable fabrication and patterning of 2D and 3D nanoparticle architectures.

articles.title: Facile hBN-hBN Interfacial Overlap Engineering for Enhanced Quantum Emitter Formation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum emitters in two-dimensional materials, particularly hBN, are promising platforms for quantum technologies. However, achieving high-density emitters at predetermined locations while preserving optical quality remains challenging. Here, we introduce a facile, cost-effective double-layer all-dry transfer approach to deterministically create overlap regions between hBN flakes. These pre-defined capped regions exhibit a significantly enhanced emitter density, with up to a 15-fold increase compared to uncapped areas. Importantly, this method does not compromise emitter quality: emitters within overlap regions demonstrate excellent optical performance, including high signal-to-background and signal-to-noise ratios, large Debye-Waller factors, high brightness, and strong spectral stability. Possible defect configurations are also discussed to contextualize the observed emission characteristics. This scalable strategy enables preferential formation of quantum emitters in targeted regions, achieving higher densities than simple treatments such as plasma irradiation while avoiding the complexity of advanced fabrication techniques. The approach provides a practical pathway for integrating high-quality quantum emitters into scalable quantum photonic platforms.

articles.title: Photo-induced Wavelength-tuning of Telecom-band Quantum Dot Nanowires Embedded in a Phase Change Material
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalable quantum-photonic technologies require spatially separated emitters to emit at the same wavelength, yet epitaxially grown quantum dots naturally exhibit emitter-to-emitter variations in their emission energies. Here, we demonstrate a contact-free post-growth tuning approach for InAs quantum dots embedded in InP nanowires using the photo-induced transformation of an amorphous Sb2S3 shell. This photoinduced effect leads to a progressive relaxation of the strain imposed on the InP core, enabling controlled spectral tuning of the quantum-dot emission. The effect is observed both at room temperature and under cryogenic conditions for quantum dots emitting in the O-band of the telecommunications spectrum. Strain-induced redshifts of approximately 7 meV at room temperature and 28 meV under cryogenic conditions are observed, respectively.
